title: Activision Blizzard hit with new sexual assault, harassment claims in lawsuit
summary: The video game publisher’s HR department — previously alleged to have condoned a “frat boy culture” — was dismissive of the plaintiff’s complaints, she claimed.

title: Ignoring a doctor’s note can be costly, EEOC reminds employers
summary: Employers should “leave the work of identifying pregnancy-related risks and limitations to qualified medical professionals,” the agency said in conciliating two separate cases.

title: This week in 5 numbers: Amazon will give grocery benefits to workers
summary: Here’s a roundup of numbers from the last week — including how many employers say artificial intelligence is actually slowing down the hiring process.

title: How can employers boost workers’ 401(k)s? Student loan matching.
summary: The SECURE 2.0 Act of 2022 for the first time allowed employers to match eligible employee payments on student loans.

title: Amazon ups minimum hourly starting wage to $20
summary: The e-commerce company increased pay by $1 an hour for full-time employees in core operations and added new grocery discounts.

title: Employers may not know how to explain their pay decisions, Aon says
summary: Only a third of those surveyed said they have conducted a pay remediation analysis, and only 5% could say that remediation is largely complete.

title: AI makes a mess of the tech job market
summary: An Andela analysis of almost 50,000 postings for engineering roles found mismatched skills and a proliferation of titles.

title: Why job descriptions should focus on workplace experience
summary: Qualified candidates looking to move into a role with the same title at another company may not find simply a list of basic tasks in a job opening persuasive, analysis from Monster found.

title: More than half of young workers want to switch jobs soon for better pay, benefits
summary: The share of Generation Z employees looking for greener pastures is on the rise, Robert Half found.

title: Veterans caught in the middle on anti-DEI efforts, research says
summary: The veteran cause typically attracts bipartisan support, but President Donald Trump’s anti-DEI agenda may have hurt veteran well-being overall, Rand researchers determined.
